newsitem.title: USA: Clinton mourns Shabazz, calls family.
newsitem.headline: Clinton mourns Shabazz, calls family.

text.p: President Clinton Monday mourned the death of Betty Shabazz, widow of slain civil rights leader Malcolm X, and called her family to express his sympathy.

"Hillary and I were saddened to learn of the passing of Betty Shabazz earlier today," Clinton said in a statement. "She devoted a long career to education and to uplifting women and children. She was also a loving mother and our prayers are with her family in this hour of grief."
Clinton called Shabazz's four daughters from Air Force One on a flight from San Francisco to Los Angeles to express his sympathy.

"He mentioned that he last saw her recently when she sat in his box at the Jackie Robinson tribute," White House spokesman Barry Toiv told reporters aboard the president's plane, referring to a professional baseball game in April at which the late Jackie Robinson was honoured.

Shabazz, 63, who became an educator and activist after her husband's murder, died Monday afternoon, succumbing to burns on more than 80 percent of her body in a June 1 blaze, which police say was set by her 12-year-old grandson.
Clinton was in California on a speaking and fund-raising trip.
